MUQATIL:46:35#2/r1.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:46:35#2/r1.speaker: author
MUQATIL:46:35#2/r1.claim: He links the threat to 7:70, where Hud's people demand the promised punishment if he is truthful.

MUQATIL:46:35/r1.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:46:35/r1.speaker: author
MUQATIL:46:35/r1.claim: Muhammad should endure harm and rejection as the messengers of determination did; ulul-azm means those marked by patience, including Abraham, Job, Isaac, Jacob, and Noah.

MUQATIL:46:35/r10.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:46:35/r10.speaker: author
MUQATIL:46:35/r10.claim: Only the disobedient who violate God's commands and prohibitions are destroyed.

MUQATIL:46:35/r2.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:46:35/r2.speaker: author
MUQATIL:46:35/r2.claim: Revealed on the day of Uhud, the verse tells the Prophet to be patient and not pray against his people, like Adam, whose resolve failed (20:115).

MUQATIL:46:35/r3.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:46:35/r3.speaker: author
MUQATIL:46:35/r3.claim: Abraham endured being cast into fire; Noah endured rejection and beatings that made him faint, then prayed for his people to be forgiven.

MUQATIL:46:35/r4.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:46:35/r4.speaker: author
MUQATIL:46:35/r4.claim: Isaac endured the sacrifice, Jacob his blindness and grief for Joseph in the pit and prison, and Job endured affliction.

MUQATIL:46:35/r5.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:46:35/r5.speaker: author
MUQATIL:46:35/r5.claim: Jonah ibn Matta endured the whale's belly; other prophets also endured affliction.

MUQATIL:46:35/r6.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:46:35/r6.speaker: author
MUQATIL:46:35/r6.claim: Twelve prophets in Jerusalem accepted punishment rather than have Israel punished for its treatment of John son of Zechariah; earthly kings killed them by sawing, flaying, impaling, burning, and crushing their heads.

MUQATIL:46:35/r7.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:46:35/r7.speaker: author
MUQATIL:46:35/r7.claim: The Prophet is told to endure as these prophets did, since worse befell them than befell him.

MUQATIL:46:35/r8.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:46:35/r8.speaker: author
MUQATIL:46:35/r8.claim: Do not press Meccan unbelievers for punishment when they ask when the promise will come; when they see it, worldly life will seem no longer than a day or part of a day.

MUQATIL:46:35/r9.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:46:35/r9.speaker: author
MUQATIL:46:35/r9.claim: Balāgh means conveying the message; the affair is a warning, while the punishment they rushed toward is a painful wind, as in 7:70.

ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p219#3/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p219#3/r1.speaker: قتادة
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p219#3/r1.claim: Qatada identifies the resolute messengers as Noah, Abraham, Moses, and Jesus.

AKHFASH:v2p519#2/r1.author: al-Akhfash al-Awsaṭ
AKHFASH:v2p519#2/r1.speaker: author
AKHFASH:v2p519#2/r1.claim: بلاغ means: that is a communication or message.

AKHFASH:v2p519#2/r2.author: al-Akhfash al-Awsaṭ
AKHFASH:v2p519#2/r2.speaker: بعضهم
AKHFASH:v2p519#2/r2.claim: Some say al-balagh is the Quran, since admonition is delivered through the Quran; the following بلاغ then restates that point.

TUSTARI:46:35/r1.author: Sahl al-Tustarī
TUSTARI:46:35/r1.speaker: author
TUSTARI:46:35/r1.claim: The verse calls for the patience of people of spiritual knowledge: the messengers before endured contentedly and submissively, without complaint or despair.

TUSTARI:46:35/r2.author: Sahl al-Tustarī
TUSTARI:46:35/r2.speaker: author
TUSTARI:46:35/r2.claim: Sahl counts twelve resolute prophets: Abraham accepted fire and the sacrifice of his son; Job endured affliction; Ishmael accepted sacrifice; Noah endured denial; Jonah prayed in the whale; Joseph remained unchanged through well and prison; Jacob lost sight and child but complained only to God.

TAB-FULL:v21p176#3/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v21p176#3/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v21p176#3/r1.claim: The Prophet must persist in his heavy mission and take the resolute messengers as examples, enduring his people's mockery, harm, and hardship as they did.

TAB-FULL:v21p176#3/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v21p176#3/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v21p176#3/r2.claim: One view defines the resolute messengers as those tested for God's sake whose trials only increased their determination, such as Noah, Abraham, and Moses.

TAB-FULL:v21p176#3/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v21p176#3/r3.speaker: عطاء الخراساني
TAB-FULL:v21p176#3/r3.claim: ʿAṭāʾ al-Khurāsānī lists Noah, Abraham, Moses, Jesus, and Muhammad among the resolute messengers.

TAB-FULL:v21p176#3/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v21p176#3/r4.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v21p176#3/r4.claim: Qatada says they used to teach that Abraham was among the resolute messengers.

TAB-FULL:v21p176#3/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v21p176#3/r5.speaker: ابن زيد
TAB-FULL:v21p176#3/r5.claim: Ibn Zayd says every messenger had resolve, since God chose no messenger without it.

TAB-FULL:v21p176#3/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v21p176#3/r6.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
TAB-FULL:v21p176#3/r6.claim: Saʿīd ibn Jubayr says God named them “those of resolve” because of their great determination.

TAB-FULL:v21p177/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v21p177/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v21p177/r1.claim: The Prophet must not ask that punishment be hastened against his people, since the promised punishment will certainly arrive.

TAB-FULL:v21p177/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v21p177/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v21p177/r2.claim: When they see the promised punishment, its severity will make worldly life seem only an hour of one day, as in 23:113.

TAB-FULL:v21p177/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v21p177/r3.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v21p177/r3.claim: One reading of “balāgh” treats it as the sufficient, limited term of their worldly stay, with “that stay” understood elliptically.

TAB-FULL:v21p177/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v21p177/r4.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v21p177/r4.claim: Another reading takes “balāgh” as the Qur'an and reminder, sufficient for them if they reflect and take heed.

TAB-FULL:v21p179/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v21p179/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v21p179/r1.claim: God destroys only those who violate his command, abandon obedience, and disbelieve; the meaning is that only the disobedient people are destroyed.

TAB-FULL:v21p179/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v21p179/r2.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v21p179/r2.claim: Qatada says only a doomed person who turns away from Islam, or a hypocrite who professes belief but acts against it, is destroyed.

TAB-FULL:v21p179/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v21p179/r3.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
TAB-FULL:v21p179/r3.claim: A Prophetic report says good intentions earn one reward, good deeds ten, bad intentions nothing unless acted on, and an enacted sin can be erased; only the utterly doomed perish.

ZAJJAJ:v4p447/r1.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v4p447/r1.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v4p447/r1.claim: Exegetes identify the resolute messengers as Noah, Abraham, Moses, Jesus, and Muhammad.

ZAJJAJ:v4p447/r2.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v4p447/r2.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v4p447/r2.claim: In “a proclamation,” nominative balāgh means “that is a proclamation”; accusative balāghan is good Arabic but differs from the muṣḥaf, understood as “they attain a proclamation.”

ZAJJAJ:v4p447/r3.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v4p447/r3.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v4p447/r3.claim: The accusative is explained by an implicit verb, as in “God’s ordinance upon you,” understood as God prescribed it as an ordinance.

ZAJJAJ:v4p447/r4.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v4p447/r4.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v4p447/r4.claim: Given God’s mercy and bounty, only the sinful people perish; an alternate vocalized reading of the verb would be valid, though he knows no one who read it that way.

ZAJJAJ:v4p447/r5.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v4p447/r5.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v4p447/r5.claim: He calls this verse the strongest possible assurance of hope in God’s mercy.

IBNABIHATIM:v10p3297/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3297/r1.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3297/r1.claim: The Prophet says this world does not befit Muhammad and his family; God required the messengers of resolve to endure hardship and renounce what they loved, and he vows to strive to do likewise.

NAHHAS:v4p175/r2.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v4p175/r2.speaker: قولان
NAHHAS:v4p175/r2.claim: Balāgh can mean a little provision or mean that what they were admonished with is sufficient; some identify it with the Qur’an.

NAHHAS:v4p175/r3.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v4p175/r3.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v4p175/r3.claim: Balāgh can be nominative under an implied ‘that is a message,’ or accusative as a verbal noun or adjective of sāʿah; only the sinful people are destroyed.

NAHHAS:v4p175/r4.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v4p175/r4.speaker: قوم
NAHHAS:v4p175/r4.claim: Some call this one of the Qur’an’s most hope-giving verses; Ibn Abbas instead identifies ‘Your Lord is forgiving to people despite their wrongdoing.’

SULAMI:v2p245#4/r1.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p245#4/r1.speaker: سهل
SULAMI:v2p245#4/r1.claim: The resolute messengers endured distinct trials: Abraham accepted fire and sacrifice, Job affliction, Ishmael sacrifice, Noah abuse, Jonah the whale, Joseph prison and the pit, and Jacob blindness and losing his son, complaining only to God.

SULAMI:v2p245#4/r2.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p245#4/r2.speaker: الواسطي
SULAMI:v2p245#4/r2.claim: The resolute are people of determination; destiny often opposes human wishes and plans, the world is founded on trials, and patience is their only remedy.

SULAMI:v2p245#4/r3.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p245#4/r3.speaker: الواسطي
SULAMI:v2p245#4/r3.claim: When hardship is reduced to an hour of a day, the good or evil done during that brief span is negligible beside divine generosity.

THALABI:v9p25/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v9p25/r1.speaker: author
THALABI:v9p25/r1.claim: One view says all prophets are people of resolve except Jonah, who left his people in anger and haste and was tested by the giants, a wolf, and the whale.

THALABI:v9p25/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v9p25/r2.speaker: الحسين بن الفضل
THALABI:v9p25/r2.claim: Al-Husayn ibn al-Fadl selects the eighteen noble prophets named in 6:83–87, since 6:90 immediately commands following their guidance.

THALABI:v9p25/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v9p25/r3.speaker: الكلبي
THALABI:v9p25/r3.claim: Al-Kalbi identifies the resolute messengers as those commanded to fight, openly declare their position, and strive against the unbelievers.

THALABI:v9p25/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v9p25/r4.speaker: بعض أهل العلم
THALABI:v9p25/r4.claim: Some scholars name twelve prophets sent to Israel who chose to suffer God's punishment rather than let it fall on Israel, after which earthly kings tortured them.

THALABI:v9p25/r5.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v9p25/r5.speaker: author
THALABI:v9p25/r5.claim: Another list names six: Noah, Hud, Salih, Lot, Shuayb, and Moses, linked to their sequential mention in al-A'raf and al-Shu'ara.

THALABI:v9p25/r6.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v9p25/r6.speaker: author
THALABI:v9p25/r6.claim: Another view limits the resolute messengers to the five law-bearing prophets: Noah, Abraham, Moses, Jesus, and Muhammad.

THALABI:v9p25/r7.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v9p25/r7.speaker: مقاتل
THALABI:v9p25/r7.claim: Muqatil names six who endured distinct trials: Noah's beatings, Abraham's fire, Isaac's sacrifice, Jacob's lost son and sight, Joseph's pit and prison, and Job's affliction.

THALABI:v9p26#2/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v9p26#2/r1.speaker: author
THALABI:v9p26#2/r1.claim: The Prophet is told not to hasten the punishment, which will inevitably come; the promised event will make earthly life seem like only an hour.

THALABI:v9p26#2/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v9p26#2/r2.speaker: author
THALABI:v9p26#2/r2.claim: One explanation says the terror of what they see will make them forget how long they lived; another says the hour is short compared with Resurrection Day.

THALABI:v9p26#2/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v9p26#2/r3.speaker: author
THALABI:v9p26#2/r3.claim: 'A message delivered' means the Quran and its exposition, which Muhammad conveyed from God, with a parallel in Surah Ibrahim.

THALABI:v9p26#2/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v9p26#2/r4.speaker: author
THALABI:v9p26#2/r4.claim: Only people who leave God's command are destroyed by the punishment when it comes.

THALABI:v9p26#2/r5.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v9p26#2/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
THALABI:v9p26#2/r5.claim: Ibn Abbas recommends writing the verse and accompanying devotional words, washing the writing, and giving the water to a woman whose labor is difficult.

THALABI:v9p26/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v9p26/r1.speaker: الحسن البصري
THALABI:v9p26/r1.claim: Hasan al-Basri names Abraham, Moses, David, and Jesus, illustrating their resolve through submission, trust, prolonged repentance, and detachment from worldly building.

THALABI:v9p26/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v9p26/r2.speaker: author
THALABI:v9p26/r2.claim: The Prophet is told to imitate Abraham's truthfulness, Moses' trust in God's aid, David's concern over past error, and Jesus' renunciation of worldly life.

THALABI:v9p26/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v9p26/r3.speaker: قتادة
THALABI:v9p26/r3.claim: Qatada identifies the resolute messengers as Noah, Abraham, Moses, and Jesus.

THALABI:v9p26/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v9p26/r4.speaker: أبو العالية
THALABI:v9p26/r4.claim: Abu al-Aliya names Noah, Abraham, and Hud, with Muhammad as the fourth, commanded to endure as they did.

THALABI:v9p26/r5.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v9p26/r5.speaker: الأحوص بن حكيم
THALABI:v9p26/r5.claim: Al-Ahwas ibn Hakim reports a city of white pearl in Eden reserved for resolute messengers, martyrs, and fighters because of their intelligence, forbearance, devotion, and understanding.

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p287/r1.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p287/r1.speaker: السدي والكلبي
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p287/r1.claim: The resolute messengers are prophets commanded to fight.

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p287/r10.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p287/r10.speaker: عبد العزيز
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p287/r10.claim: One list names Noah, Hud, Abraham, Shuayb, and Moses.

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p287/r11.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p287/r11.speaker: السدي
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p287/r11.claim: One list names Abraham, Moses, David, Solomon, Jesus, and Muhammad.

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p287/r12.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p287/r12.speaker: ابن جريج
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p287/r12.claim: Another list includes Ishmael, Jacob, Job, but excludes Jonah, Solomon, and Adam.

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p287/r13.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p287/r13.speaker: عائشة عن النبي
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p287/r13.claim: Aisha reports God approved the resolute messengers for patience through adversity and hidden trials.

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p287/r14.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p287/r14.speaker: مقاتل
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p287/r14.claim: Not hastening means not praying against them.

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p287/r15.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p287/r15.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p287/r15.claim: Alternatively, it means do not hasten punishment; this is a threat.

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p287/r16.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p287/r16.speaker: يحيى
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p287/r16.claim: What they will see is the promised punishment.

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p287/r17.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p287/r17.speaker: النقاش
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p287/r17.claim: Alternatively, what they will see is the Hereafter.

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p287/r18.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p287/r18.speaker: يحيى
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p287/r18.claim: Brief tarrying means in the world until punishment came.

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p287/r19.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p287/r19.speaker: النقاش
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p287/r19.claim: Alternatively, it means their stay in graves until raised for judgment.

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p287/r20.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p287/r20.speaker: ابن عيسى
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p287/r20.claim: Balāgh means the brief stay itself is a sufficient warning.

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p287/r21.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p287/r21.speaker: الحسن
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p287/r21.claim: Balāgh means this Qur'an is a message.

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p287/r22.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p287/r22.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p287/r22.claim: It may mean the outcome warns of destruction in this world or punishment in the next.

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p287/r23.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p287/r23.speaker: يحيى
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p287/r23.claim: The transgressing people who alone perish are polytheists.

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p287/r24.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p287/r24.speaker: مقاتل
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p287/r24.claim: The verse came to Muhammad at Uhud to console and steady him after suffering.

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p287/r3.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p287/r3.speaker: الحسن
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p287/r3.claim: They are prophets who suffered no trial.

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p287/r4.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p287/r4.speaker: ابن جريج
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p287/r4.claim: They are prophets afflicted with hardship without sin.

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p287/r6.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p287/r6.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p287/r6.claim: They may be those who patiently endured their people's abuse without despair.

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p287/r7.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p287/r7.speaker: ابن زيد
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p287/r7.claim: One view includes all prophets among the resolute.

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p287/r8.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p287/r8.speaker: أبو العالية
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p287/r8.claim: One list names Noah, Hud, and Abraham, with Muhammad the fourth.

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p287/r9.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p287/r9.speaker: ابن عباس
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p287/r9.claim: One list names Noah, Abraham, Moses, and Jesus.

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p290/r1.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p290/r1.speaker: ابن عباس وقتادة
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p290/r1.claim: They say Surah Muhammad is Medinan except one verse revealed after Hajj as the Prophet left Mecca, looked back at the House, and wept; that verse begins 'How many a town was stronger than your town.'

WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p204/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p204/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p204/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas, through Ata and Abu Salih, identifies the resolute messengers as Noah, Abraham, Moses, and Jesus; Maʿmar transmits a similar view from Qatada.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p204/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p204/r2.speaker: أبو العالية
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p204/r2.claim: Abu al-Aliya names Noah, Abraham, and Hud, with Muhammad as the fourth.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p204/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p204/r3.speaker: الحسن
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p204/r3.claim: Al-Hasan names Abraham, Moses, David, and Jesus, explaining each one's trial and steadfastness.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p204/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p204/r4.speaker: مقاتل
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p204/r4.claim: Muqatil counts six: Noah, Abraham, Isaac, Jacob, Joseph, and Job, each patient through a distinct ordeal.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p204/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p204/r5.speaker: الكلبي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p204/r5.claim: Al-Kalbi says they were commanded to fight and openly struggled in God's religion.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p204/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p204/r6.speaker: أهل المعاني والمحققون
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p204/r6.claim: The scholars of meaning and critical scholars say all messengers are people of resolve, since every messenger is resolute, firm, judicious, and fully rational.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p204/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p204/r7.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p204/r7.claim: The particle من clarifies the class of messengers rather than selecting only some of them, like saying garments made of brocade; their resolve is shown in patience and composure.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p204/r8.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p204/r8.speaker: ابن زيد
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p204/r8.claim: Ibn Zayd holds that all the messengers are included among the people of resolve.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p206/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p206/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p206/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas says the omitted object of do not hurry for them is their punishment; the Prophet had become weary and wanted punishment for those refusing him, so he was ordered to be patient.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p206/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p206/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p206/r2.claim: Their promised punishment is in the afterlife, when they will feel as if they stayed only an hour of a day.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p206/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p206/r3.speaker: الكلبي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p206/r3.claim: Al-Kalbi says the hour-like stay refers to their time in the graves.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p206/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p206/r4.speaker: مقاتل
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p206/r4.claim: Muqatil says the hour-like stay refers to worldly life.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p206/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p206/r5.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p206/r5.claim: At the sight of punishment, the long stay in worldly life and the intermediate realm seems like a day-hour or nothing at all; what has passed is as though it never was.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p206/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p206/r6.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p206/r6.claim: The author cites a verse comparing what has passed to something that never existed, and what is coming to something already present.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p206/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p206/r7.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p206/r7.claim: The author takes بلاغ as the Quran's communication from God to people, beginning a new sentence; this is the exegetes' and reciters' view.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p206/r8.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p206/r8.speaker: مقاتل
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p206/r8.claim: Muqatil instead takes بلاغ as their having reached only an hour-like duration; the author prefers the preceding explanation.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p207/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p207/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p207/r1.claim: The فسق people are disobedient and outside God's command; the punishment reaches them after Muhammad has conveyed God's message.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p207/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p207/r2.speaker: قوم
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p207/r2.claim: Some people say no verse gives greater hope for God's mercy than this one.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p207/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p207/r3.speaker: أبو إسحاق
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p207/r3.claim: Abu Ishaq explains that, despite God's mercy and favor, only the transgressing people are destroyed.

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:46:35/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:46:35/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:46:35/r1.claim: All messengers had resolve except Jonah; another view restricts the resolute messengers to the law-bearing Noah, Abraham, Moses, Jesus, and Muhammad.

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:46:35/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:46:35/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:46:35/r2.claim: Disbelievers will experience their worldly lifetime as only an hour of a day from the terror they witness and forget its length; this Qur'an is God's message, and only the disobedient perish.

JISHUMI:v9p6429/r10.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v9p6429/r10.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v9p6429/r10.claim: Resolve can also mean obligations, strength and patience, or preparation; deliberation prepares for an affair while resolve carries it through.

JISHUMI:v9p6429/r11.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v9p6429/r11.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v9p6429/r11.claim: Resolve is a particular kind of will, not a separate faculty from will.

JISHUMI:v9p6429/r9.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v9p6429/r9.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v9p6429/r9.claim: Resolve is a firm commitment in the heart; ʿazama ʿalayka can mean I adjure you, or I command you emphatically.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p271#2/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p271#2/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p271#2/r2.claim: The possessors of resolve are people of firmness.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p271#2/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p271#2/r3.speaker: الضحاك
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p271#2/r3.claim: They are people of seriousness and patience.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p271#2/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p271#2/r4.speaker: ابن زيد
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p271#2/r4.claim: All messengers had resolve and judgment; “from” indicates kind rather than a subset.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p271#2/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p271#2/r5.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p271#2/r5.claim: Other lists identify them as all except Jonah, the eighteen named in al-Anʿām, those ordered to fight, six named in other sūrahs, or six exemplars of patience.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p271#2/r6.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p271#2/r6.speaker: مقاتل
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p271#2/r6.claim: His six are Noah, Abraham, Isaac, Jacob, Joseph, and Job, each enduring a distinct trial.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p271#2/r7.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p271#2/r7.speaker: ابن عباس وقتادة
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p271#2/r7.claim: They are the five lawgivers: Noah, Abraham, Moses, Jesus, and Muhammad.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p271#2/r8.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p271#2/r8.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p271#2/r8.claim: The author supports the five by the verses specifying the covenant-bearing prophets and the religion prescribed to Noah.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p271#2/r9.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p271#2/r9.speaker: عائشة
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p271#2/r9.claim: The Prophet says this world is unfit for him and his family, and God required from him the patience required of the possessors of resolve.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p272/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p272/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p272/r1.claim: Muhammad should not hasten the punishment; he may have grown impatient for it to fall on those who refused.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p272/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p272/r2.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p272/r2.claim: When they see the punishment, worldly and grave residence seems like an hour because the past seems not to have existed.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p272/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p272/r3.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p272/r3.claim: “A proclamation” means the Qur’an and its explanation are a message from God.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p272/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p272/r4.speaker: الزجاج
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p272/r4.claim: Only transgressors perish under God’s mercy and grace; some call this the strongest verse for hope.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p317/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p317/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p317/r1.claim: Ulu al-ʿazm means messengers of resolve, steadfastness and patience.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p317/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p317/r2.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p317/r2.claim: If min is partitive, the resolute messengers include Noah, Abraham, Isaac, Jacob, Joseph, Job, Moses, David and Jesus, each enduring the trials listed.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p317/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p317/r3.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p317/r3.claim: Alternatively, min explains the phrase, so all messengers are resolute; 20:115 says Adam lacked resolve and 68:48 warns against the Companion of the Fish.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p317/r4.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p317/r4.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p317/r4.claim: Do not ask that Quraysh’s punishment be hastened: it will surely come, and then they will deem their worldly stay no more than an hour.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p317/r5.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p317/r5.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p317/r5.claim: “A conveyance” may mean that the warning is sufficient admonition, or that it is the Messenger’s delivery.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p317/r6.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p317/r6.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p317/r6.claim: Readings include balagha, balaghan, two forms of yahlak, and nahlik with first-person plural.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p317/r7.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p317/r7.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p317/r7.claim: Only the immoral people are destroyed.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p317/r8.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p317/r8.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p317/r8.claim: A report promises ten good deeds for every grain of sand in the world to whoever recites Surat al-Ahqaf.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p106#2/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p106#2/r3.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p106#2/r3.claim: The patience command follows the report of the disbelievers' fate: since this is their end with God, Muhammad should be patient with his mission and fear no one for God's sake.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p106#2/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p106#2/r4.speaker: عطاء الخراساني وغيره
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p106#2/r4.claim: They take min as partitive: the resolute messengers are those who endured particular hardship with their peoples, such as Noah, Abraham, Moses, and Jesus.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p106#2/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p106#2/r5.speaker: ابن زيد
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p106#2/r5.claim: Ibn Zayd takes min as explanatory: all messengers have resolve, while the wording highlights the messengers among all people of resolve to honor them as Muhammad's finest model.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p106#2/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p106#2/r6.speaker: أبو القاسم الحكيم
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p106#2/r6.claim: Abū al-Qāsim al-Ḥakīm says every messenger is among the resolute except Jonah.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p106#2/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p106#2/r7.speaker: الحسن بن الفضل
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p106#2/r7.claim: Al-Ḥasan ibn al-Faḍl identifies the resolute as the eighteen named in Sūrat al-Anʿām, followed by the instruction to follow their guidance.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p106#2/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p106#2/r8.speaker: مقاتل
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p106#2/r8.claim: Muqātil names six: Noah endured his people, Abraham endured people, Isaac accepted sacrifice, Jacob endured Joseph's loss, Joseph endured pit and prison, and Job endured affliction.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p107/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p107/r1.speaker: النبي عليه السلام
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p107/r1.claim: The Prophet prayed that God show mercy to Moses, who endured more harm than this and remained patient; Ibn ʿAṭiyya adds that every prophet necessarily has resolve and patience.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p107/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p107/r2.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p107/r2.claim: Do not hasten punishment for the disbelievers or resent their long life: when they see punishment, the world will seem no longer than an hour because elapsed time becomes nothing.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p107/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p107/r3.speaker: أبي بن كعب
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p107/r3.claim: Ubayy ibn Kaʿb reads sāʿatan min al-nahār, an hour of the day.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p107/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p107/r4.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p107/r4.claim: The majority reads balāgh in the nominative: it may mean this Quran and law are a warning and conveyance, or that the short worldly stay was their only allotted provision; another parse omits a predicate.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p107/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p107/r5.speaker: أبو مجلز
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p107/r5.claim: Abū Mujliz stops at la tastaʿjil and starts a new sentence with balāgh, taking its predicate from the earlier lahum; others object to the long separation.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p107/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p107/r6.speaker: الحسن بن أبي الحسن وعيسى
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p107/r6.claim: Al-Ḥasan and ʿĪsā read balāghan in the accusative; it fits the first two nominative interpretations but not Abū Mujliz's parsing and assumes an omitted verb.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p108/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p108/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p108/r1.claim: Most read fa-hal yuhlaku passively; some transmit an active reading, which Abū al-Fatḥ regards as undesirable, while Zayd ibn Thābit reports the passive with al-qawm al-fāsiqīn accusative.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p108/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p108/r2.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p108/r2.claim: The passage is pure warning: good deeds earn tenfold, evil deeds onefold, and God promises Paradise for obedience and the Fire for disbelief, so only the doomed perish.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p108/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p108/r3.speaker: الثعلبي
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p108/r3.claim: Al-Thaʿlabī transmits that this is the Quran's most hopeful verse for believers.

TABRISI:46:35/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:46:35/r1.speaker: ابن زيد
TABRISI:46:35/r1.claim: If min is explanatory, all prophets are people of resolve because each accepted the mission and bore its burdens; most commentators and the apparent Imami reports instead take it partitively.

TABRISI:46:35/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:46:35/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
TABRISI:46:35/r2.claim: The best-known view identifies five lawgiving messengers whose new law superseded the earlier one: Noah, Abraham, Moses, Jesus, and Muhammad; reports from al-Baqir and al-Sadiq call them the leading prophets.

TABRISI:46:35/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:46:35/r3.speaker: مقاتل
TABRISI:46:35/r3.claim: Mujahid identifies six people of resolve by the trials they endured: Noah, Abraham, Isaac, Jacob, Joseph, and Job.

TABRISI:46:35/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:46:35/r4.speaker: السدي
TABRISI:46:35/r4.claim: Al-Suddi and al-Kalbi define them as those commanded to fight who openly confronted and struggled in religion; Abu al-Aliya instead names Abraham, Hud, Noah, and Muhammad.

TABRISI:46:35/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:46:35/r5.speaker: author
TABRISI:46:35/r5.claim: ʿAzm denotes obligation and firm resolve, and people of resolve are those who established laws and required people to follow them.

TABRISI:46:35/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:46:35/r6.speaker: author
TABRISI:46:35/r6.claim: The Prophet must not hurry their punishment, which is certain and near; when they see it, their long life in this world and the intermediate state will seem like one hour.

TABRISI:46:35/r7.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:46:35/r7.speaker: author
TABRISI:46:35/r7.claim: Balāgh may mean the Quran and its explanation as a communication from God, or may refer to that short duration as a sufficient announcement.

TABRISI:46:35/r8.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:46:35/r8.speaker: قتادة
TABRISI:46:35/r8.claim: The punishment befalls only the disobedient; Qatada further limits the destroyed to a polytheist who turned away from Islam or a hypocrite who affirmed with his tongue but acted otherwise.

TABRISI:46:35/r9.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:46:35/r9.speaker: الزجاج
TABRISI:46:35/r9.claim: Al-Zajjaj says nothing offers stronger hope in God’s mercy than the assurance that only the wicked perish.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p392/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p392/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p392/r1.claim: Ulū al-ʿazm means people of resolve and endurance.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p392/r10.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p392/r10.speaker: الحسين بن الفضل
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p392/r10.claim: A ninth view identifies the eighteen prophets named at 6:83–86.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p392/r11.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p392/r11.speaker: الثعلبي
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p392/r11.claim: A tenth view includes all prophets except Jonah.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p392/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p392/r2.speaker: الضحاك عن ابن عباس ومجاهد وقتادة وعطاء الخراساني وابن السائب
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p392/r2.claim: One view identifies them as Noah, Abraham, Moses, Jesus, and Muhammad.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p392/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p392/r3.speaker: أبو العالية الرياحي
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p392/r3.claim: A second view lists Noah, Hud, Abraham, and Muhammad.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p392/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p392/r4.speaker: الحسن
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p392/r4.claim: A third view means prophets who were not subjected to a trial.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p392/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p392/r5.speaker: مجاهد والشعبي
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p392/r5.claim: A fourth view identifies them as Arab prophets.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p392/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p392/r6.speaker: السدي
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p392/r6.claim: A fifth view lists Abraham, Moses, David, Solomon, Jesus, and Muhammad.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p392/r7.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p392/r7.speaker: ابن جريج
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p392/r7.claim: A sixth view includes Ishmael, Jacob, and Job, but excludes Adam, Jonah, and Solomon.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p392/r8.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p392/r8.speaker: ابن السائب والسدي
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p392/r8.claim: A seventh view identifies those commanded to wage jihad and fight.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p392/r9.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p392/r9.speaker: ابن زيد وابن الأنباري
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p392/r9.claim: An eighth view includes all messengers; Ibn Zayd states this, and Ibn al-Anbari chooses it because من marks the class rather than a subset.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p393/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p393/r1.speaker: بعض المفسرين
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p393/r1.claim: The Prophet was weary and wished punishment on those who rejected him, so he was commanded to be patient.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p393/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p393/r2.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p393/r2.claim: The deniers will see the promised punishment and feel they had remained in worldly life only an hour, since the past will seem as if it never existed.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p393/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p393/r3.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p393/r3.claim: Alternatively, the worldly stay is called an hour because it is short beside their residence in the afterlife's punishment.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p393/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p393/r4.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p393/r4.claim: The word balāgh may mean conveying the message, or sufficiency: what was disclosed gives them enough warning and guidance.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p393/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p393/r5.speaker: ابن جرير
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p393/r5.claim: Another parsing takes balāgh as their allotted period in worldly life, with the words meaning that this is their brief stay until their appointed terms.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p393/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p393/r6.speaker: أبو العالية وأبو عمران
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p393/r6.claim: They read balāgh as balagh, with a doubled lām and no alif.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p394/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p394/r1.speaker: أبو رزين وأبو المتوكل وابن محيصن
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p394/r1.claim: They read yuhlaku with an open yāʾ and kasra on the lām, meaning that the sinful people alone perish when they see the punishment.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p394/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p394/r2.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p394/r2.claim: The sinful people are those who depart from God's command.

RAZI-FULL:v28p30#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v28p30#2/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v28p30#2/r1.claim: After establishing oneness, prophethood, and resurrection and answering objections, God consoles the Prophet, whom unbelievers were troubling, by commanding patience like that of the messengers.

RAZI-FULL:v28p30#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v28p30#2/r2.speaker: بعض المفسرين
RAZI-FULL:v28p30#2/r2.claim: One view takes min as partitive and identifies the resolute messengers as a subset, naming Noah, Abraham, Isaac, Jacob, Joseph, Job, Moses, David, and Jesus, with Adam and Jonah as counterexamples.

RAZI-FULL:v28p30#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v28p30#2/r3.speaker: الأكثرون من المفسرين
RAZI-FULL:v28p30#2/r3.claim: The other view says all messengers possess resolve, firmness, sound judgment, completeness, and reason; min is explanatory, meaning the messengers before you.

RAZI-FULL:v28p30#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v28p30#2/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v28p30#2/r4.claim: The omitted object of 'do not hasten' is their punishment; the Prophet had grown distressed and wished punishment for those who refused, so he was told it would surely come, and then worldly and intermediate life would seem only an hour.

RAZI-FULL:v28p31/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v28p31/r1.speaker: الشاعر
RAZI-FULL:v28p31/r1.claim: A poetic line illustrates how a long past span seems as if it never existed, just as what arrives seems as if it had always been.

RAZI-FULL:v28p31/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v28p31/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v28p31/r2.claim: Balāgh may mean that this admonition is sufficient, or that it is a message delivered by the messengers; only those who abandon heedfulness and its demands are destroyed.

QURTUBI-FULL:46:35#2/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:46:35#2/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:46:35#2/r1.claim: Abraham answered “Submit” by submitting to the Lord of the worlds and remained truthful through trials of wealth, child, homeland, and self.

QURTUBI-FULL:46:35#2/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:46:35#2/r10.speaker: يحيى
QURTUBI-FULL:46:35#2/r10.claim: The promise they see is punishment; they seem to have spent only an hour in worldly life before it arrived.

QURTUBI-FULL:46:35#2/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:46:35#2/r11.speaker: النقاش
QURTUBI-FULL:46:35#2/r11.claim: Al-Naqqāsh identifies the promise as the afterlife and says their apparent hour is the period spent in their graves before resurrection.

QURTUBI-FULL:46:35#2/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:46:35#2/r12.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:46:35#2/r12.claim: Another explanation is that the horror of what they see makes their long worldly stay seem short.

QURTUBI-FULL:46:35#2/r13.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:46:35#2/r13.speaker: الحسن
QURTUBI-FULL:46:35#2/r13.claim: Al-Ḥasan says balāgh means this Quran is a message or conveyance; its nominative case assumes an omitted subject.

QURTUBI-FULL:46:35#2/r14.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:46:35#2/r14.speaker: ابن عيسى
QURTUBI-FULL:46:35#2/r14.claim: Ibn ʿĪsā takes balāgh to mean that the brief stay itself is sufficient as a warning; pause placement then may fall after balāgh or nahār.

QURTUBI-FULL:46:35#2/r15.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:46:35#2/r15.speaker: أبو حاتم
QURTUBI-FULL:46:35#2/r15.claim: Abū Ḥātim reports a reader pausing after “do not hasten” and starting “for them” as a phrase meaning they have a message.

QURTUBI-FULL:46:35#2/r16.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:46:35#2/r16.speaker: ابن الأنباري
QURTUBI-FULL:46:35#2/r16.claim: Ibn al-Anbārī rejects that pause because it separates the lām from balāgh and attaches it to an unrelated governor.

QURTUBI-FULL:46:35#2/r17.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:46:35#2/r17.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:46:35#2/r17.claim: Balāghan may be accusative as a verbal noun or modifier of hour, or genitive as a modifier of day; ʿĪsā ibn ʿUmar and al-Ḥasan read the accusative.

QURTUBI-FULL:46:35#2/r18.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:46:35#2/r18.speaker: قراءة بعض القراء
QURTUBI-FULL:46:35#2/r18.claim: Some recite baligh as an imperative, pausing after “day” and beginning with the command to convey.

QURTUBI-FULL:46:35#2/r19.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:46:35#2/r19.speaker: ابن عباس وغيره
QURTUBI-FULL:46:35#2/r19.claim: The wrongdoers who perish are those who depart from God's command.

QURTUBI-FULL:46:35#2/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:46:35#2/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:46:35#2/r2.claim: Moses' resolve is illustrated by his declaration that God is the Lord of his people and their forefathers.

QURTUBI-FULL:46:35#2/r20.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:46:35#2/r20.speaker: ابن محيصن
QURTUBI-FULL:46:35#2/r20.claim: Ibn Muḥayṣin reads the verb with the people as its grammatical subject, rather than leaving the verb passive.

QURTUBI-FULL:46:35#2/r21.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:46:35#2/r21.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:46:35#2/r21.claim: He recommends writing the verse and a supplication on a page, washing it, and giving it to a woman struggling in childbirth to drink.

QURTUBI-FULL:46:35#2/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:46:35#2/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:46:35#2/r3.claim: David erred, was admonished, and wept in repentance for forty years beneath a tree grown from his tears.

QURTUBI-FULL:46:35#2/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:46:35#2/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:46:35#2/r4.claim: Jesus' resolve is shown by refusing to build worldly structures, saying the world is a crossing to pass through rather than inhabit.

QURTUBI-FULL:46:35#2/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:46:35#2/r5.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:46:35#2/r5.claim: The Prophet is urged to match Abraham's truthfulness, Moses' trust in divine help, David's concern over past lapses, and Jesus' renunciation of worldly life.

QURTUBI-FULL:46:35#2/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:46:35#2/r6.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:46:35#2/r6.claim: One view says this patience command was abrogated by the sword verse; Qurtubi says that is more apparent because the surah is Meccan.

QURTUBI-FULL:46:35#2/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:46:35#2/r7.speaker: مقاتل
QURTUBI-FULL:46:35#2/r7.claim: Muqātil says this verse came to the Prophet on the day of Uḥud to comfort and steady him after his injury.

QURTUBI-FULL:46:35#2/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:46:35#2/r8.speaker: مقاتل
QURTUBI-FULL:46:35#2/r8.claim: Do not hasten for them means do not pray against them; another view says do not hasten their punishment, whose furthest delay is Resurrection.

QURTUBI-FULL:46:35#2/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:46:35#2/r9.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:46:35#2/r9.claim: The object of hastening is omitted and understood to be the punishment.

QURTUBI-FULL:46:35#3/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:46:35#3/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:46:35#3/r1.claim: The quotation from al-Nāziʿāt likewise says people will feel they had stayed only an evening or its morning when they see Resurrection.

QURTUBI-FULL:46:35#3/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:46:35#3/r2.speaker: قتادة
QURTUBI-FULL:46:35#3/r2.claim: Qatāda says only someone doomed, an unbeliever, perishes.

QURTUBI-FULL:46:35#3/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:46:35#3/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:46:35#3/r3.claim: An unnamed view calls this the strongest verse concerning hope.

QURTUBI-FULL:46:35/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:46:35/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:46:35/r1.claim: He defines the resolute messengers as people of resolve and patience.

QURTUBI-FULL:46:35/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:46:35/r10.speaker: الحسن بن الفضل
QURTUBI-FULL:46:35/r10.claim: He chooses that list because the following verse commands the Prophet to follow their guidance.

QURTUBI-FULL:46:35/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:46:35/r11.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:46:35/r11.claim: A further view says all messengers are resolute; ʿAlī ibn Mahdī al-Ṭabarī prefers it and takes min as generic, not partitive.

QURTUBI-FULL:46:35/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:46:35/r12.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:46:35/r12.claim: An alternative excludes Jonah from all prophets of resolve because he left his people in anger and the Prophet was warned not to imitate his haste; Abū al-Qāsim al-Ḥakīm relates trials involving plunder, a wolf, and the whale.

QURTUBI-FULL:46:35/r13.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:46:35/r13.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:46:35/r13.claim: Another account says twelve Israelite prophets in Syria chose to bear God's punishment themselves rather than let it fall on the disobedient Israelites; rulers tortured and killed them in several ways.

QURTUBI-FULL:46:35/r14.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:46:35/r14.speaker: الحسن
QURTUBI-FULL:46:35/r14.claim: Al-Ḥasan identifies four resolute messengers: Abraham, Moses, David, and Jesus.

QURTUBI-FULL:46:35/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:46:35/r2.speaker: مجاهد
QURTUBI-FULL:46:35/r2.claim: Mujāhid lists five lawgiving messengers: Noah, Abraham, Moses, Jesus, and Muhammad.

QURTUBI-FULL:46:35/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:46:35/r3.speaker: أبو العالية
QURTUBI-FULL:46:35/r3.claim: Abū al-ʿĀliya lists Noah, Hūd, and Abraham, and says God asked the Prophet to be the fourth.

QURTUBI-FULL:46:35/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:46:35/r4.speaker: السدي
QURTUBI-FULL:46:35/r4.claim: Al-Suddī names six: Abraham, Moses, David, Solomon, Jesus, and Muhammad.

QURTUBI-FULL:46:35/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:46:35/r5.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:46:35/r5.claim: Another list is Noah, Hūd, Ṣāliḥ, Shuʿayb, Lot, and Moses, the sequence named in al-Aʿrāf and al-Shuʿarāʾ.

QURTUBI-FULL:46:35/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:46:35/r6.speaker: مقاتل
QURTUBI-FULL:46:35/r6.claim: Muqātil lists six examples of endurance: Noah endured his people, Abraham the fire, Isaac sacrifice, Jacob loss of son and sight, Joseph the well and prison, and Job affliction.

QURTUBI-FULL:46:35/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:46:35/r7.speaker: ابن جريج
QURTUBI-FULL:46:35/r7.claim: Ibn Jurayj includes Ishmael, Jacob, and Job, while excluding Jonah, Solomon, and Adam.

QURTUBI-FULL:46:35/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:46:35/r8.speaker: الشعبي والكلبي ومجاهد
QURTUBI-FULL:46:35/r8.claim: They say the resolute are messengers ordered to fight who openly confronted and fought the disbelievers.

QURTUBI-FULL:46:35/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:46:35/r9.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:46:35/r9.claim: One interpretation identifies eighteen notable messengers from al-Anʿām as the people of resolve.

BAYDAWI-FULL:46:35/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:46:35/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:46:35/r1.claim: Those of resolve are steadfast and serious; من may explain the group or indicate some of them, and the Prophet belongs to their company.

BAYDAWI-FULL:46:35/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:46:35/r2.speaker: قيل
BAYDAWI-FULL:46:35/r2.claim: One view identifies the resolute as law-bearing prophets who established and defended their laws despite hardship: Noah, Abraham, Moses, and Jesus.

BAYDAWI-FULL:46:35/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:46:35/r3.speaker: قيل
BAYDAWI-FULL:46:35/r3.claim: Another view includes those patient under trials: Noah’s abuse, Abraham’s fire and attempted sacrifice, Jacob’s loss and blindness, Joseph’s well and prison, Job’s affliction, David’s forty years of weeping, and Jesus’ simple life; Moses quotes 26:61–62.

BAYDAWI-FULL:46:35/r4.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:46:35/r4.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:46:35/r4.claim: Do not hurry Quraysh’s punishment; it will certainly arrive at its appointed time.

BAYDAWI-FULL:46:35/r5.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:46:35/r5.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:46:35/r5.claim: When they see the promised punishment, its terror will make their worldly stay seem no longer than an hour.

BAYDAWI-FULL:46:35/r6.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:46:35/r6.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:46:35/r6.claim: بلاغ may mean the admonition or sura is sufficient, the Messenger’s delivery (supported by بلغ), or a promised term they reach; the reading with accusative means they delivered a message.

BAYDAWI-FULL:46:35/r7.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:46:35/r7.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:46:35/r7.claim: The doomed are those who depart from taking heed or obedience; variant readings include passive/active يَهْلِك and first-person plural with القوم accusative.

BAYDAWI-FULL:46:35/r8.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:46:35/r8.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
BAYDAWI-FULL:46:35/r8.claim: A report promises ten good deeds for each grain of sand in the world to whoever recites Sūrat al-Aḥqāf; no grading is stated.

NASAFI-FULL:v4p143#7/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p143#7/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p143#7/r1.claim: Ulū al-ʿazm are resolute, steadfast messengers; “from the messengers” may be partitive, identifying those named in 33:7.

NASAFI-FULL:v4p143#7/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p143#7/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p143#7/r2.claim: That partitive view excludes Jonah, because the Prophet is told not to be like the companion of the fish, and excludes Adam for lacking resolve; alternatively, “from” explains that all messengers are resolute.

NASAFI-FULL:v4p143#7/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p143#7/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p143#7/r3.claim: Do not hasten Quraysh's punishment: it will reach them even if delayed, and they will then count earthly life as only an hour.

NASAFI-FULL:v4p143#7/r4.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p143#7/r4.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p143#7/r4.claim: “A message” may mean the admonition is sufficient, or that this is the Messenger's act of conveying it.

NASAFI-FULL:v4p143#7/r5.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p143#7/r5.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p143#7/r5.claim: Only disobedient polytheists who refuse to heed and act on the reminder perish in punishment.

NASAFI-FULL:v4p143#7/r6.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p143#7/r6.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p143#7/r6.claim: A report promises ten good deeds per grain of sand in the world for whoever recites Sūrat al-Aḥqāf.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p428#3/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p428#3/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p428#3/r1.claim: Al-Ahqaf is a long, raised sand dune with a bend; the verb ihqawqafa means to become crooked, as witnessed by Imruʾ al-Qays's line.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p428#3/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p428#3/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p428#3/r2.claim: The word ʿaniya describes being perplexed about a matter when its direction is unknown; it may assimilate to ʿayya, as illustrated by a poetic line about a dove confused over its egg.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p428#3/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p428#3/r3.speaker: ابن عباس وقتادة
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p428#3/r3.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas and Qatada say the passage about the revelation being from God and the command to be patient are Medinan, while the rest of the surah is Meccan.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p451/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p451/r10.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p451/r10.claim: أولو العزم means messengers of firm resolve and endurance in struggle; من may be partitive, identifying some messengers, or explanatory, identifying all messengers as people of resolve.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p451/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p451/r9.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p451/r9.claim: The command to be patient connects to the disbelievers' fate just described: this is their condition before God, so the Prophet should endure and not fear or hasten their punishment.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p452#2/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p452#2/r1.speaker: أبو الفتح
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p452#2/r1.claim: Abū al-Fatḥ calls the referenced wording undesirable.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p452#2/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p452#2/r2.speaker: زيد بن ثابت
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p452#2/r2.claim: Zayd ibn Thābit reads يهلك with ḍamma on the initial yāʾ and kasra on the lām.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p452#2/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p452#2/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p452#2/r3.claim: He parses القوم الفاسقون in the accusative and says the verse warns and threatens.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p452/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p452/r1.speaker: عطاء الخراساني والكلبي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p452/r1.claim: Ata al-Khurasani and al-Kalbi take من as partitive; Ibn Zayd takes it as explanatory, so all messengers are people of resolve.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p452/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p452/r2.speaker: الحسن بن الفضل
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p452/r2.claim: Hasan ibn al-Fadl identifies the resolute ones as the eighteen named in Surat al-An'am because the Prophet was told to follow their guidance.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p452/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p452/r3.speaker: مقاتل
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p452/r3.claim: Muqatil names six: Noah endured his people, Abraham the fire, Isaac the sacrifice, Jacob separation and blindness, Joseph the well and prison, and Job affliction; others add Moses, David, and Jesus with their trials.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p452/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p452/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p452/r4.claim: The Prophet must not pray for Quraysh's punishment to be hastened: it will certainly arrive, and then their perceived worldly stay will seem no longer than an hour.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p452/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p452/r5.speaker: أبي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p452/r5.claim: Ubayy reads من النهار, while the majority read من نهار.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p452/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p452/r6.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p452/r6.claim: The majority read بلاغ in the nominative as a predicate of an omitted subject, referring to their brief worldly stay; alternatively it means the Qur'an's proclamation. Abu Mujliz's analysis making it the subject with لهم as predicate and stopping at فلا تستعجل is rejected because it breaks the clause connection.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p452/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p452/r7.speaker: الحسن، وزيد بن علي، وعيسى
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p452/r7.claim: They read بلاغا in the accusative, understood as a proclamation delivered or made; Abu Suraah and Abu Mujliz read بلغ addressing the Prophet, supporting the proclamation sense, and Abu Mujliz also has a past-tense reading.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p452/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p452/r8.speaker: الجمهور
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p452/r8.claim: The majority read يهلك with a passive stem; Ibn Muhaysin is reported with an active form, in two vowel variants, from the dialect هلك بكسر اللام.

SAMIN-DURR:46:35/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:46:35/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:46:35/r1.claim: The fāʾ connects this clause to what precedes, with an evident causal relation.

SAMIN-DURR:46:35/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:46:35/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:46:35/r2.claim: من الرسل may be partitive, distinguishing messengers with resolve from others, or explanatory, making all messengers people of resolve.

SAMIN-DURR:46:35/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:46:35/r3.speaker: قيل
SAMIN-DURR:46:35/r3.claim: With nominative بلاغ, one parse supplies a topic such as that hour or the Quran and law; another makes it a topic with لهم as predicate, but that parse is very weak because of an intervening clause.

SAMIN-DURR:46:35/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:46:35/r4.speaker: زيد بن علي والحسن وعيسى
SAMIN-DURR:46:35/r4.claim: They read بلاغا in the accusative as a verbal noun, بلغ بلاغا, supported by Abu Majliz's reading بلغ أمرا; Makkī also allows an adjective of ساعة.

SAMIN-DURR:46:35/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:46:35/r5.speaker: الحسن
SAMIN-DURR:46:35/r5.claim: Al-Hasan also reads بلاغ in the genitive as an adjective of نهار through an omitted noun, or as an emphatic description of time.

SAMIN-DURR:46:35/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:46:35/r6.speaker: العامة
SAMIN-DURR:46:35/r6.claim: The common يهلك is passive; Ibn Muhaysin has an active reading, with a further dialectal vowel form, and Ibn Jinni calls both disfavored.

SAMIN-DURR:46:35/r7.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:46:35/r7.speaker: زيد بن ثابت
SAMIN-DURR:46:35/r7.claim: Zayd ibn Thabit reads يهلك with a passive prefix but active meaning, God as subject and القوم as object; another reading has نهلك with nūn.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p304#2/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p304#2/r3.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p304#2/r3.claim: The Prophet must endure his people’s denial as the resolute messengers endured the denial of their peoples.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p304#2/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p304#2/r4.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p304#2/r4.claim: The best-known enumeration of the resolute messengers is Noah, Abraham, Moses, Jesus, and Muhammad, whom God names in al-Ahzab and al-Shura.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p304#2/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p304#2/r5.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p304#2/r5.claim: Another possible reading takes all messengers as resolute, with min explaining the class rather than selecting some members; God knows best.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p304#2/r6.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p304#2/r6.speaker: عائشة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p304#2/r6.claim: She reports that the Prophet endured successive fasting days and said God required from him the same patience required of the resolute messengers, over hardship and what they loved.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p305#2/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p305#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p305#2/r1.claim: God destroys only those who deserve destruction and punishment; this is an expression of His justice.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p305/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p305/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p305/r1.claim: The Prophet is told not to hasten the punishment of his opponents, as in commands to leave deniers respite.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p305/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p305/r2.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p305/r2.claim: On seeing the promised Judgment, people will regard their residence in the world and the intermediate realm as only an hour, given the ordeal and length of that Day.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p305/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p305/r3.speaker: ابن جرير
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p305/r3.claim: Ibn Jarir offers two readings of “a proclamation”: it may describe their stay as sufficient, or identify the Qur’an itself as the proclamation.

BIQAI-FULL:v7p145/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p145/r4.speaker: القشيري
BIQAI-FULL:v7p145/r4.claim: Al-Qushayrī defines patience as standing firm under God's decree without complaint or resistance.

BIQAI-FULL:v7p145/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p145/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v7p145/r5.claim: The Prophet's command to be patient resumes the call to endure the hardships of conveying the message.

BIQAI-FULL:v7p146/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p146/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v7p146/r1.claim: The most apparent reading makes min partitive: “the resolute messengers” are foremost law-bearing messengers who established their laws, commonly Noah, Abraham, Moses, Jesus, and Muhammad.

BIQAI-FULL:v7p146/r10.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p146/r10.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v7p146/r10.claim: The surah's close connects back to its opening warning and proofs, and links its themes of resurrection, creation, revelation, divine power, and wisdom into a coherent ending.

BIQAI-FULL:v7p146/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p146/r2.speaker: ابن زيد
BIQAI-FULL:v7p146/r2.claim: Ibn Zayd says the phrase means all messengers; Ibn al-Anbārī adopts this view and takes min as generic rather than partitive.

BIQAI-FULL:v7p146/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p146/r3.speaker: الثعلبي
BIQAI-FULL:v7p146/r3.claim: Al-Thaʿlabī transmits the view that all prophets are meant except Jonah.

BIQAI-FULL:v7p146/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p146/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v7p146/r4.claim: The identities of the resolute messengers are disputed, but the partitive interpretation is the most famous and, in the author's judgment, clearest.

BIQAI-FULL:v7p146/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p146/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v7p146/r5.claim: The Prophet must not hasten the opponents' punishment or act against them before the proper time; this restrains haste, a grave vice, and completes the virtue of patience.

BIQAI-FULL:v7p146/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p146/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v7p146/r6.claim: The promised event may be seen at death or in the afterlife; it warns sinners and gives good news to the obedient, who will feel worldly life lasted only a brief hour.

BIQAI-FULL:v7p146/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p146/r7.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v7p146/r7.claim: The phrase “an hour of daylight” both verifies the short duration and belittles it, since sāʿa can otherwise mean a long period.

BIQAI-FULL:v7p146/r8.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p146/r8.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v7p146/r8.claim: The Quran is a clear, sufficient warning that guides people to the Mighty and Wise's lasting reward; those it does not guide are people whom God has ordained for misery.

BIQAI-FULL:v7p146/r9.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p146/r9.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v7p146/r9.claim: Only the deeply rebellious are destroyed; the passive form focuses on the outcome and signals that their destruction is easy for God.

DURR-FULL:v7p453#2/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p453#2/r1.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v7p453#2/r1.claim: Aisha reports the Prophet's endurance of fasting and hardship: God required the resolute messengers and Muhammad to bear what they disliked and forgo what they loved.

DURR-FULL:v7p453#2/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p453#2/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v7p453#2/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas identifies the resolute messengers as Muhammad, Noah, Abraham, Moses, and Jesus.

DURR-FULL:v7p453#2/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p453#2/r3.speaker: أبو العالية
DURR-FULL:v7p453#2/r3.claim: Abu al-Aliyah lists Noah, Hud, and Abraham, with Muhammad as the fourth; their examples show them openly separating from their people's polytheism.

DURR-FULL:v7p453#2/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p453#2/r4.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v7p453#2/r4.claim: Qatada lists Noah, Hud, Abraham, Shuayb, and Moses as the resolute messengers.

DURR-FULL:v7p453#2/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p453#2/r5.speaker: ابن جريج
DURR-FULL:v7p453#2/r5.claim: Ibn Jurayj lists Ishmael, Jacob, and Job as resolute, while excluding Adam, Jonah, and Solomon.

DURR-FULL:v7p455/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p455/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v7p455/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas says the resolute messengers were those commanded to fight until they had carried it through: Noah, Hud, Salih, Moses, David, and Solomon.

DURR-FULL:v7p455/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p455/r2.speaker: جابر بن عبد الله
DURR-FULL:v7p455/r2.claim: Jabir reports that the resolute messengers numbered 313.

DURR-FULL:v7p455/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p455/r3.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v7p455/r3.claim: Qatada says only a culpable unbeliever is destroyed: either a polytheist who turns his back on Islam or a hypocrite whose heart contradicts his profession.

DURR-FULL:v7p455/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p455/r4.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v7p455/r4.claim: Anas transmits a prayer for success that invokes God's mercy, forgiveness, safety, good deeds, Paradise, and deliverance from Hell, and includes the two verses about the briefness of worldly time.

BURSEVI:v8p383/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p383/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p383/r1.claim: ‘Resolve’ means earnest intention and firm purpose; given the unbelievers’ fate, the Prophet must patiently endure them as the steadfast messengers, indeed as one of their foremost.

BURSEVI:v8p383/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p383/r2.speaker: التكملة
BURSEVI:v8p383/r2.claim: Al-Takmila reads ‘of the messengers’ as explanatory, making every messenger a person of resolve and steadfastness.

BURSEVI:v8p383/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p383/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p383/r3.claim: The author rejects the explanatory reading because it would erase the verse’s distinction of a special group.

BURSEVI:v8p383/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p383/r4.speaker: الأسئلة المقحمة
BURSEVI:v8p383/r4.claim: The sound view takes ‘of’ partitively: the resolute are lawbearing messengers who established their laws and endured hardship and opposition, especially Noah, Abraham, Moses, Jesus, and Muhammad.

BURSEVI:v8p383/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p383/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p383/r5.claim: A poem lists Noah, Abraham, Moses, Jesus, and Muhammad as the resolute messengers.

BURSEVI:v8p383/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p383/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p383/r6.claim: Another view defines the resolute by their trials: Noah endured beatings, Abraham fire and the attempted sacrifice, Jacob loss, Joseph the pit and prison, Job illness, Moses fear of capture, Jonah the whale, David forty years of weeping, and Jesus renunciation of worldly building.

BURSEVI:v8p383/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p383/r7.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p383/r7.claim: Some exclude Jonah for haste and Adam for lacking resolve, citing the commands not to be like the Companion of the Fish and Adam’s failure to keep his covenant.

BURSEVI:v8p384#2/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p384#2/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p384#2/r1.claim: The Prophet is told not to hasten punishment for Mecca’s unbelievers, which is near; despite his impatience, they are granted time for worldly pleasures before severe punishment.

BURSEVI:v8p384#2/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p384#2/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p384#2/r2.claim: When they see the promised punishment, their worldly stay will seem only an hour because its terror and duration make them forget it; even a long past will seem nearly nonexistent.

BURSEVI:v8p384#2/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p384#2/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p384#2/r3.claim: The final outcome of bodily pleasure is spiritual torment in the intermediate realm and bodily punishment at Resurrection.

BURSEVI:v8p384#2/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p384#2/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p384#2/r4.claim: A Persian couplet urges the listener to notice the swiftly passing caravan of life and the racing horses of night and day.

BURSEVI:v8p384#3/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p384#3/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p384#3/r1.claim: ‘A warning’ may be the predicate of an omitted subject, meaning the admonition suffices, or it may mean the Messenger’s delivery; a slave needs the stick, while a free person understands a gesture.

BURSEVI:v8p384#3/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p384#3/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p384#3/r2.claim: ‘Will any perish?’ is rhetorical for ‘none will perish,’ meaning none will be destroyed by the punishment that descends except the disobedient.

BURSEVI:v8p384#3/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p384#3/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p384#3/r3.claim: The disobedient are those who leave admonition and obedience; an esoteric reading identifies them as people who abandon seeking God for other aims, making the passage a direct threat.

BURSEVI:v8p384#3/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p384#3/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
BURSEVI:v8p384#3/r4.claim: A report in al-Firdaws, attributed to Ibn Abbas from the Prophet, prescribes writing this verse and using its washed ink for a woman experiencing difficult childbirth.

BURSEVI:v8p384#4/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p384#4/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
BURSEVI:v8p384#4/r1.claim: A report in Ayn al-Ma‘ani says that, for difficult childbirth, two verses are written on a sheet, washed, and given to the woman to drink, with water sprinkled on her abdomen and vulva.

BURSEVI:v8p384#4/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p384#4/r2.speaker: شرعة الإسلام
BURSEVI:v8p384#4/r2.claim: Shari‘at al-Islam prescribes writing a Quranic invocation and the verse on a clean glass or silver dish, washing it, and giving the water to a woman in difficult labor.

BURSEVI:v8p384#4/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p384#4/r3.speaker: عيسى ابن مريم
BURSEVI:v8p384#4/r3.claim: A story says Jesus prayed for a cow whose calf was stuck, ‘Creator of a soul from a soul, free her,’ and she delivered; the same writing is prescribed for women and animals.

BURSEVI:v8p384#4/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p384#4/r4.speaker: آكام المرجان
BURSEVI:v8p384#4/r4.claim: Akam al-Marjan permits writing scripture or divine remembrance in lawful ink for an afflicted or ill person, washing it, and giving it to drink, citing Ahmad and others.

BURSEVI:v8p384#4/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p384#4/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p384#4/r5.claim: The permission excludes unknown foreign religious-language writing that might contain disbelief, impure ink such as blood, and rearranging or reversing Qur’anic letters, all of which are forbidden.

BURSEVI:v8p384#4/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p384#4/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p384#4/r6.claim: The surah ends with decisive punishment that eradicates the unbelievers, followed by praise to God forever.

ALUSI-FULL:v26p34#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v26p34#2/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v26p34#2/r1.claim: The initial faʾ can answer an implicit condition: given the unbelievers' fate, or God's demonstrated power, endure what they inflict.

ALUSI-FULL:v26p34#2/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v26p34#2/r10.speaker: ابن عباس
ALUSI-FULL:v26p34#2/r10.claim: One report from Ibn ʿAbbās counts six messengers commanded to fight: Noah, Hūd, Ṣāliḥ, Moses, David, and Solomon.

ALUSI-FULL:v26p34#2/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v26p34#2/r11.speaker: مقاتل
ALUSI-FULL:v26p34#2/r11.claim: Muqātil's six are Noah, Abraham, Isaac, Jacob, Joseph, and Job.

ALUSI-FULL:v26p34#2/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v26p34#2/r12.speaker: قتادة
ALUSI-FULL:v26p34#2/r12.claim: A report from Qatāda counts five: Noah, Hūd, Abraham, Shuʿayb, and Moses.

ALUSI-FULL:v26p34#2/r13.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v26p34#2/r13.speaker: قتادة
ALUSI-FULL:v26p34#2/r13.claim: Another report from Qatāda counts four: Noah, Abraham, Moses, and Jesus; al-Ālūsī calls this the soundest view.

ALUSI-FULL:v26p34#2/r14.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v26p34#2/r14.speaker: السيوطي
ALUSI-FULL:v26p34#2/r14.claim: Al-Suyūṭī calls the five-person view soundest: those four plus Muḥammad, citing a report from Ibn ʿAbbās and authorities of the Prophet's household.

ALUSI-FULL:v26p34#2/r15.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v26p34#2/r15.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v26p34#2/r15.claim: Al-Ālūsī says the five are not the verse's intended list, since the command would then ask the Prophet to imitate his own patience.

ALUSI-FULL:v26p34#2/r16.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v26p34#2/r16.speaker: أبو العالية
ALUSI-FULL:v26p34#2/r16.claim: A report attributed to Abū al-ʿĀliya counts Noah, Abraham, Hūd, and the Messenger as a fourth.

ALUSI-FULL:v26p34#2/r17.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v26p34#2/r17.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v26p34#2/r17.claim: Al-Ālūsī favors the explanatory reading, urging patience as the messengers generally endured; the term later commonly denotes the famous five.

ALUSI-FULL:v26p34#2/r18.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v26p34#2/r18.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v26p34#2/r18.claim: The Prophet should not ask for the punishment of Meccan unbelievers to be hastened; it is near to falling upon them.

ALUSI-FULL:v26p34#2/r19.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v26p34#2/r19.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v26p34#2/r19.claim: When they see the promised punishment, its severity makes their time in the world seem no longer than a brief hour of a day.

ALUSI-FULL:v26p34#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v26p34#2/r2.speaker: البحر
ALUSI-FULL:v26p34#2/r2.claim: Al-Baḥr treats the faʾ as joining this sentence to earlier reports about the afterlife: their state is thus, so do not hurry and fear only God.

ALUSI-FULL:v26p34#2/r20.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v26p34#2/r20.speaker: أبي
ALUSI-FULL:v26p34#2/r20.claim: Ubayy reads “from the day” with the definite article.

ALUSI-FULL:v26p34#2/r21.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v26p34#2/r21.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v26p34#2/r21.claim: Balāgh can be an omitted-subject predicate meaning that the admonition suffices, or mean a communication by the Messenger; the reference might be the Qurʾān or the sūra.

ALUSI-FULL:v26p34#2/r22.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v26p34#2/r22.speaker: أبو مجلز، أبو سراج الهذلي
ALUSI-FULL:v26p34#2/r22.claim: Abū Majlaz and Abū Sirāj al-Hudhalī read balagh as an imperative, “convey,” supporting the communication interpretation.

ALUSI-FULL:v26p34#2/r23.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v26p34#2/r23.speaker: أبو مجلز
ALUSI-FULL:v26p34#2/r23.claim: In another transmission Abū Majlaz reads ballagha in the past tense; Abū Ḥayyān instead favors the brief sojourn as the referent of balāgh, like “brief enjoyment.”

ALUSI-FULL:v26p34#2/r24.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v26p34#2/r24.speaker: أبو مجلز
ALUSI-FULL:v26p34#2/r24.claim: Abū Majlaz also parses balāgh as a nominative subject whose predicate is the earlier lahum; al-Ālūsī calls this very weak because it interrupts the apparent syntax.

ALUSI-FULL:v26p34#2/r25.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v26p34#2/r25.speaker: الحسن، زيد بن علي، عيسى
ALUSI-FULL:v26p34#2/r25.claim: Al-Ḥasan, Zayd ibn ʿAlī, and ʿĪsā read accusative balāghan, with an implied verb such as “convey a communication.”

ALUSI-FULL:v26p34#2/r26.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v26p34#2/r26.speaker: الحسن، زيد بن علي، عيسى
ALUSI-FULL:v26p34#2/r26.claim: These readers also transmit a genitive reading, making balāgh an adjective for “day.”

ALUSI-FULL:v26p34#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v26p34#2/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v26p34#2/r3.claim: A number of commentators instead take the faʾ as joining this sentence to the preceding passage, with a clear causal force.

ALUSI-FULL:v26p34#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v26p34#2/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v26p34#2/r4.claim: ʿAzm can mean firm resolve and exertion in an affair, or patience in it.

ALUSI-FULL:v26p34#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v26p34#2/r5.speaker: ابن زيد، الجبائي، جماعة
ALUSI-FULL:v26p34#2/r5.claim: On the explanatory reading of min, all messengers are possessors of resolve: they persist in conveying revelation and patiently accept God's commands and decrees.

ALUSI-FULL:v26p34#2/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v26p34#2/r6.speaker: عطاء الخراساني، الحسن بن الفضل، الكلبي، مقاتل، قتادة، أبو العالية، ابن جريج
ALUSI-FULL:v26p34#2/r6.claim: Most exegetes take min as partitive, meaning that only some messengers are the possessors of resolve; they differ over who and how many.

ALUSI-FULL:v26p34#2/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v26p34#2/r7.speaker: الحسن بن الفضل
ALUSI-FULL:v26p34#2/r7.claim: Al-Ḥasan ibn al-Faḍl counts eighteen, identified with the prophets named in al-Anʿām, followed by the command to follow their guidance.

ALUSI-FULL:v26p34#2/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v26p34#2/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v26p34#2/r8.claim: One unnamed view counts nine: Noah, Abraham, the son intended for sacrifice, Jacob, Joseph, Job, Moses, David, and Jesus, each noted for a trial endured.

ALUSI-FULL:v26p34#2/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v26p34#2/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v26p34#2/r9.claim: Another unnamed view counts seven: Adam, Noah, Abraham, Moses, David, Solomon, and Jesus.

ALUSI-FULL:v26p35/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v26p35/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v26p35/r1.claim: The last clause warns that only those who leave admonition or obedience are destroyed.

ALUSI-FULL:v26p35/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v26p35/r2.speaker: ابن محيصن
ALUSI-FULL:v26p35/r2.claim: Ibn Muḥayṣin is reported by Ibn Khālawayh with two forms of the verb yahlik; Abū al-Fatḥ calls the form with kasra in the past rare and disfavored.

ALUSI-FULL:v26p35/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v26p35/r3.speaker: زيد بن ثابت
ALUSI-FULL:v26p35/r3.claim: Zayd ibn Thābit reads nahlik with the majestic first-person plural and puts “the sinful people” in the accusative.

ALUSI-FULL:v26p35/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v26p35/r4.speaker: أنس
ALUSI-FULL:v26p35/r4.claim: Al-Ṭabarānī in al-Duʿāʾ transmits from Anas, from the Prophet, a supplication for a need to be fulfilled that includes these verses and asks for mercy, forgiveness, relief, payment of debts, and every worldly and otherworldly need.

ALUSI-FULL:v26p36/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v26p36/r1.speaker: علي
ALUSI-FULL:v26p36/r1.claim: Ibn Mardawayh reports that ʿAlī said Sūrat Muḥammad was revealed concerning Banū Umayya.

ALUSI-FULL:v26p36/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v26p36/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v26p36/r2.claim: Al-Ālūsī doubts that the report about Banū Umayya is sound.

ALUSI-FULL:v26p36/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v26p36/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v26p36/r3.claim: Al-Ālūsī says Banū Umayya fall under the Qurʾān's general descriptions of unbelievers.

ALUSI-FULL:v26p36/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v26p36/r4.speaker: author
