ALUSI-FULL:v26p36/r4.claim: Likewise, the Prophet's household fall under the general descriptions of believers.

ALUSI-FULL:v26p36/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v26p36/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v26p36/r5.claim: Al-Ālūsī condemns whoever severs family ties and harms the Prophet's household.

ALUSI-FULL:v26p36/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v26p36/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v26p36/r6.claim: He says no more should be said beyond this general inclusion, except to condemn harm to the Prophet's household.

ELMALILI:46:30-35/r10.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:46:30-35/r10.speaker: author
ELMALILI:46:30-35/r10.claim: The Prophet is to be patient like the resolute messengers because he is one of them; azm means decisive commitment and steadfast pursuit of one’s purpose.

ELMALILI:46:30-35/r11.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:46:30-35/r11.speaker: author
ELMALILI:46:30-35/r11.claim: The phrase may mean all messengers, since every prophet is resolute, or a subset distinguished by establishing law and enduring hardship; their famous names appear in Q 33:7.

ELMALILI:46:30-35/r12.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:46:30-35/r12.speaker: author
ELMALILI:46:30-35/r12.claim: The author also accepts that every prophet named in the Qur’an is among the resolute, since other messengers were not named in the Qur’an.

ELMALILI:46:30-35/r13.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:46:30-35/r13.speaker: author
ELMALILI:46:30-35/r13.claim: The Prophet should not hasten punishment for the disbelievers, especially the Quraysh; on seeing judgment, their worldly years will seem no longer than an hour because of the terror and length of the afterlife.

ELMALILI:46:30-35/r14.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:46:30-35/r14.speaker: author
ELMALILI:46:30-35/r14.claim: Balāgh can mean either a sufficient, eloquent admonition or an eloquent conveyance, so no one can claim not to have heard the warning.

ELMALILI:46:30-35/r15.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:46:30-35/r15.speaker: author
ELMALILI:46:30-35/r15.claim: Ultimately only rebellious people who leave obedience and refuse admonition are destroyed.

ELMALILI:46:30-35/r16.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:46:30-35/r16.speaker: النبي ﷺ عن أنس
ELMALILI:46:30-35/r16.claim: Al-Ṭabarānī transmits from Anas that the Prophet advised reciting a supplication containing these verses when one asks for a need and wants it granted; no grading is stated.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v26p67/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v26p67/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v26p67/r1.claim: Ulu al-ʿazm means people marked by resolve: a firmly formed intention to act or speak without hesitation; the author cites Quranic usage and Saʿd b. Nashib’s verse.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v26p67/r10.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v26p67/r10.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v26p67/r10.claim: The poet Murra b. ʿAdāʾ al-Faqʿasī may have drawn his image of a night seeming absent once a goal is reached from this verse.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v26p67/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v26p67/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v26p67/r2.claim: Religiously praiseworthy resolve seeks purification of the self and welfare of the community; it rests on patience through hardship, piety, and vigilant self-accounting.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v26p67/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v26p67/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v26p67/r3.claim: Adam’s lack of resolve occurred before his descent into the realm of moral obligation.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v26p67/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v26p67/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v26p67/r4.claim: On the author’s reading, min in “among the messengers” is partitive, meaning only some messengers were Ulu al-ʿazm.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v26p67/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v26p67/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNASHUR-FULL:v26p67/r5.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas says all messengers are Ulu al-ʿazm; on this view min is explanatory.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v26p67/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v26p67/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v26p67/r6.claim: The verse establishes Muhammad among Ulu al-ʿazm: the commanded comparison makes his obedient patience like theirs, and whoever bears their patience belongs among them.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v26p67/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v26p67/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v26p67/r7.claim: The prohibition concerns hastening punishment for the polytheists; delay does not conflict with resolve and lengthens the Messenger’s patience, strengthening his resolve.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v26p67/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v26p67/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v26p67/r8.claim: The omitted object of “hasten” is punishment or destruction; the lām means “for their sake,” with an omitted noun meaning hastening their destruction.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v26p67/r9.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v26p67/r9.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v26p67/r9.claim: Their seeing the promised punishment as if after only an hour explains the ban: its arrival is certain, so delay or haste does not change its occurrence.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v26p68/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v26p68/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v26p68/r1.claim: “Of a day” describes the hour: daytime seems short because people are occupied, while a sleepless night drags; the indefinite hour conveys a small span.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v26p68/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v26p68/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v26p68/r2.claim: The author compares this minimization to the Friday hour for answered prayer, which the Prophet indicated with a gesture showing its shortness.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v26p68/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v26p68/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v26p68/r3.claim: “A communication” summarizes what preceded for believers and unbelievers; it is the predicate of an omitted “this,” as in titles and document headings.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v26p68/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v26p68/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v26p68/r4.claim: The demonstrative may be stated explicitly, as in “this is a communication for people” and “in this is a message for worshippers.”

IBNASHUR-FULL:v26p68/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v26p68/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v26p68/r5.claim: The summary is a fresh introductory conclusion, comparable to the Quranic phrases “those are ten complete” and “that was a community that passed away.”

IBNASHUR-FULL:v26p68/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v26p68/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v26p68/r6.claim: The final question functions as a negation, allowing an exception: only the wicked are destroyed, as in the question about turning from Abraham’s religion.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v26p68/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v26p68/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v26p68/r7.claim: The conclusion follows from earlier statements about the Messenger, the warning to wrongdoers, and the destruction of surrounding towns: only wicked polytheists perish.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v26p69/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v26p69/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v26p69/r1.claim: Destruction is literal in accounts such as ʿĀd and figurative for the wretched condition of afterlife punishment.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v26p69/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v26p69/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v26p69/r2.claim: Definite “the people” can mean the whole class of wicked people, universalizing the warning, or the known polytheists just mentioned; the latter substitution hints that shirk causes destruction.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v26p69/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v26p69/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v26p69/r3.claim: The imperfect can combine future destruction of Meccan polytheists with the destruction of earlier nations; here wickedness means abandoning faith through shirk.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v26p69/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v26p69/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v26p69/r4.claim: The exception indicates that others escape this destruction: those who believed and acted righteously.

TABATABAI:46:33-35/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:46:33-35/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:46:33-35/r4.claim: Because resurrection is proven rationally and affirmed without doubt by God, the Prophet should endure rejection and not hasten their punishment.

TABATABAI:46:33-35/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:46:33-35/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:46:33-35/r5.claim: When deniers see the promised Resurrection and punishment, their worldly stay will seem to them no longer than an hour of a day.

TABATABAI:46:33-35/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:46:33-35/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:46:33-35/r6.claim: The Qur'an is God's message delivered through prophethood, and only the disobedient who leave servitude are destroyed by it.

TABATABAI:46:35#2/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:46:35#2/r3.speaker: العالم عليه السلام
TABATABAI:46:35#2/r3.claim: Asked whether believing jinn enter Paradise, the Imam says God has enclosures between Paradise and Hell for believing jinn and sinful Shiites.

TABATABAI:46:35#2/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:46:35#2/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:46:35#2/r4.claim: A similar Sunni report exists; al-Qummi's report is disconnected and implicit, so if accepted the enclosures mean the lowest levels of Paradise, consistent with Qur'anic generalities.

TABATABAI:46:35#2/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:46:35#2/r5.speaker: أبو عبد الله عليه السلام
TABATABAI:46:35#2/r5.claim: Al-Kafi reports that the leading prophets and messengers are the five resolute ones: Noah, Abraham, Moses, Jesus, and Muhammad.

TABATABAI:46:35#2/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:46:35#2/r6.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم
TABATABAI:46:35#2/r6.claim: A report says Seth was the first successor on earth, every prophet had a successor, and there were 120,000 prophets including five resolute messengers.

TABATABAI:46:35#2/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:46:35#2/r7.speaker: author
TABATABAI:46:35#2/r7.claim: The identification of five resolute messengers is supported by many reports from the Prophet and the Imams al-Baqir, al-Sadiq, and al-Rida.

TABATABAI:46:35#2/r8.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:46:35#2/r8.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم
TABATABAI:46:35#2/r8.claim: Asked the time between this world and the next, the Prophet answered that it is like the blink of an eye.

TABATABAI:46:35/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:46:35/r1.speaker: بعضهم
TABATABAI:46:35/r1.claim: Another explanation is resolve to honor the covenant taken from the prophets, as the verse about Adam says he lacked resolve.

TABATABAI:46:35/r10.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:46:35/r10.speaker: بعضهم
TABATABAI:46:35/r10.claim: Two reported lists of four are Noah, Abraham, Moses, and Jesus, or Noah, Abraham, Hud, and Muhammad.

TABATABAI:46:35/r11.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:46:35/r11.speaker: author
TABATABAI:46:35/r11.claim: The competing lists either lack evidence or rely on arguments that prove nothing; earlier discussion of the resolute messengers is in volume two.

TABATABAI:46:35/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:46:35/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:46:35/r2.claim: Resolve means the determinate religious law; Ahl al-Bayt reports identify five law-bearing messengers: Noah, Abraham, Moses, Jesus, and Muhammad.

TABATABAI:46:35/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:46:35/r3.speaker: بعض المفسرين
TABATABAI:46:35/r3.claim: Some say all messengers are resolute, taking from the messengers as an explanatory phrase for those of resolve.

TABATABAI:46:35/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:46:35/r4.speaker: بعضهم
TABATABAI:46:35/r4.claim: Others identify the resolute as the eighteen prophets in 6:83–90, because God says to follow their guidance.

TABATABAI:46:35/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:46:35/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:46:35/r5.claim: The eighteen-prophet argument is misplaced: follow their guidance comes after mention of their ancestors, descendants, and brothers, not immediately after their list.

TABATABAI:46:35/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:46:35/r6.speaker: بعضهم
TABATABAI:46:35/r6.claim: One view names nine: Noah, Abraham, the sacrificed son, Jacob, Joseph, Job, Moses, David, and Jesus.

TABATABAI:46:35/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:46:35/r7.speaker: بعضهم
TABATABAI:46:35/r7.claim: Other lists give seven—Adam, Noah, Abraham, Moses, David, Solomon, and Jesus—or six who were commanded to fight: Noah, Hud, Salih, Moses, David, Solomon.

TABATABAI:46:35/r8.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:46:35/r8.speaker: بعضهم
TABATABAI:46:35/r8.claim: A different list of six is Noah, Abraham, Isaac, Jacob, Joseph, and Job.

TABATABAI:46:35/r9.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:46:35/r9.speaker: بعضهم
TABATABAI:46:35/r9.claim: Some list five as Noah, Hud, Abraham, Shuʿayb, and Moses.

ASAD-NOTES:46:35#n42/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:46:35#n42/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:46:35#n42/r1.claim: The promise they will see refers to the reality of life after death.

ASAD-NOTES:46:35#n43/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:46:35#n43/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:46:35#n43/r1.claim: The hereafter exposes earthly time as an illusion of human experience, without bearing on ultimate reality.

ASAD-NOTES:46:35#n44/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:46:35#n44/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:46:35#n44/r1.claim: Asad points to 6:47, note 37, for a parallel statement.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p283/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p283/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p283/r3.claim: The sūrah’s conclusion warns and threatens disbelievers while urging the Prophet to patience and perseverance.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p311/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p311/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p311/r2.claim: The sūrah closes by warning the disbelievers and urging the Prophet to meet their rejection with patience and forbearance.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p318/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p318/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p318/r2.claim: The Prophet must persevere like all earlier messengers, each of whom passed every trial; min in ‘the messengers’ is explanatory and inclusive, not partitive.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p318/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p318/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p318/r3.claim: The command not to hurry concerns opponents who taunt the Prophet by demanding punishment; when it arrives, their present respite will seem only an hour or day.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p318/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p318/r4.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p318/r4.claim: Balāgh is the predicate of an omitted subject, emphasizing that the Prophet’s duty is to deliver the warning fully and leave no excuse for denial; the punishment’s victims bear responsibility.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:46:35/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:46:35/r1.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:46:35/r1.claim: When the Prophet and Companions felt overwhelmed by denial and oppression, God comforted them: a lifetime's wait is negligible on the eternal scale, so reward and punishment are not delayed.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:46:35/r2.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:46:35/r2.speaker: Bazı tefsirciler
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:46:35/r2.claim: Some take “messengers of resolve” to divide prophets into resolute and non-resolute groups, and list Noah, Abraham, Moses, Jesus, and Muhammad.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:46:35/r3.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:46:35/r3.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:46:35/r3.claim: The author agrees that all prophets possess resolve; Muhammad is called to their patience and resolve, which God has also granted him.

STUDYQURAN:46:35/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:46:35/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:46:35/r1.claim: The instruction to be patient addresses the Prophet, or by extension all Muslims.

STUDYQURAN:46:35/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:46:35/r2.speaker: most scholars
STUDYQURAN:46:35/r2.claim: Most understand the resolute messengers as Noah, Abraham, Moses, Jesus, and Muhammad, who brought a new Book and revealed law.

STUDYQURAN:46:35/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:46:35/r3.speaker: Q
STUDYQURAN:46:35/r3.claim: Other proposals identify Noah, Hud, and Abraham, or all the prophets, as the resolute messengers.

STUDYQURAN:46:35/r4.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:46:35/r4.speaker: al-Tustarī
STUDYQURAN:46:35/r4.claim: Al-Tustari identifies twelve patient prophets as resolute, recounting the trials and steadfastness of Abraham, Job, Ishmael, Noah, Jonah, Joseph, and Jacob.

STUDYQURAN:46:35/r5.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:46:35/r5.speaker: JJ, Q
STUDYQURAN:46:35/r5.claim: The Prophet is told not to pray for the disbelievers' punishment to be hastened, as some prophets had done, because it would arrive in due course.

STUDYQURAN:46:35/r6.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:46:35/r6.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:46:35/r6.claim: The delay may be understood as God's mercy or as a means of reserving a greater punishment for the Hereafter.

STUDYQURAN:46:35/r7.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:46:35/r7.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:46:35/r7.claim: The reality and length of the Hereafter make worldly life seem to the disbelievers like only an hour of a day.

STUDYQURAN:46:35/r8.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:46:35/r8.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:46:35/r8.claim: The iniquitous are destroyed through punishment in the Hereafter and by being led astray, made to forget God, and distanced from Him and their true selves.

STUDYQURAN:46:intro/r12.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:46:intro/r12.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:46:intro/r12.claim: The sūrah concludes with a reminder of God's omnipotence and counsels Muhammad to follow earlier prophets who patiently endured disbelievers' insults.

STUDYQURAN:46:intro/r5.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:46:intro/r5.speaker: some commentators
